subject: Mandarin

source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design — Mandarin Grade 7 (First published 2022, Revised 2024)
source.notes: designs/Mandarin-Grade-7-Design-Formatted-April-2024.pdf already exists locally in the repo's designs/ folder (provided by the user, per repo-wide standing rule — no web search or Drive mirror needed). Title, ISBN and publisher confirmed directly from the PDF's own title page (page 1: 'KENYA INSTITUTE OF CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT ... JUNIOR SCHOOL CURRICULUM DESIGN MANDARIN GRADE 7') and imprint page (page 2: 'First published 2022 / Revised 2024 ... ISBN:978-9914-43-811-6 ... Published and printed by Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development'). Read with the Read tool with no pages parameter per environment constraints; full text extracted natively across all 77 pages in one call. Structure verified verbatim against the PDF's own 'SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUB STRANDS' table (page x) and the 27 per-theme strand tables (pages 1-58).

essenceNote: Kenya is part of the international community and therefore the learner shall be given an opportunity to learn foreign languages in addition to the national, official and indigenous languages. These foreign languages include Arabic, French, German and Mandarin. The learner is expected to acquire the four language skills: listening, speaking, reading and writing at a basic level in the non-formal curriculum ... guided by social-constructivism and environmental theories ... The learner will transit to Senior School having acquired basic proficiency equivalent to A1/YCT 2 (verbatim essence statement, page viii).

subStrands.name: Oral Expression — Pronunciation, Intonation
specificLearningOutcomes: Recall key information from audio sources and texts
Apply correct tones, pronunciation and intonation in various contexts
Acknowledge the importance of clear articulation of words in conveying meaning
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is correct pronunciation and intonation important in oral communication?
learningExperiences: Watch an audio-visual clip on informal Chinese greetings and numbers (1-100) and repeat saying them with the correct tones (吃了吗? 你今天怎么样? 你最近怎么样? 最近好吗? 大家好)
Work jointly to arrange the words and phrases in the right sequence from the audio clip
Answer questions from the oral text
Introduce oneself (informal greetings, name, age and place of residence) with appropriate pronunciation and intonation (e.g. 大家好，我叫......，我今年......岁, 我住在......)
Take turns to introduce their friends (name, age and place of residence)
Listen to an authentic text with various accents/speech patterns and repeat what they hear
Discuss the importance of understanding and respecting cultural differences in informal greetings with peers
coreCompetencies: Learning to Learn: The learner works collaboratively with others to arrange words in the right sequence.
Communication and Collaboration: The learner speaks clearly and effectively using appropriate language, expression and gestures as they introduce themselves and their friends to their peers.
linkedLearningAreas: English and Kiswahili — relating the skills of using correct tone and pronunciation to convey appropriate meaning while communicating
subStrands.notes: Register is informal (吃了吗/你今天怎么样/大家好), distinct from Grade 8's formal greetings register (您好/您贵姓). Self-introduction pattern 大家好，我叫......，我今年......岁，我住在...... is the theme's core productive sentence frame.

subStrands.name: Oral Expression — Active Listening, Vocabulary and Language Use
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify familiar words and phrases in simple conversations
Use varied and appropriate vocabulary in oral communication
Exhibit interest in using vocabulary effectively during interactions
keyInquiryQuestions: How does varied vocabulary help in effective communication?
learningExperiences: Mime or gesture different professions as their peers guess the correct title and say them aloud (老师、医生、司机、警察、护士、农民)
Listen to simple descriptions of the various professions and assign the appropriate title for each description
Team up with peers to sing the song on titles and professions of nuclear family members (爸爸、妈妈、哥哥、弟弟、姐姐、妹妹、外公、外婆、奶奶、爷爷)
Work jointly to introduce members of their nuclear family (name, age and profession)
Take turns to answer questions related to the name, age and profession of their nuclear family (e.g. 你们家有几口人? 爷爷做什么工作?)
Make short presentations of their preferred professions to their peers
Explore how parents can provide guidance regarding their future career paths and aspirations
coreCompetencies: Citizenship: The learner demonstrates tolerance and understanding of different viewpoints as they acknowledge and respect the diverse professional aspirations of their peers.
Communication and collaboration: The learner speaks effectively and logically when they make short presentations of their nuclear family members.
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — the concept of making choices and professional aspirations
subStrands.notes: Nuclear family (10 titles: 爸爸/妈妈/哥哥/弟弟/姐姐/妹妹/外公/外婆/奶奶/爷爷 — distinguishing maternal 外公/外婆 from paternal 爷爷/奶奶) plus 6 professions (老师/医生/司机/警察/护士/农民).

subStrands.name: Oral Expression — Vocabulary Development, Articulation
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify familiar and unfamiliar words in a variety of contexts
Express views and opinions using acquired vocabulary
Appreciate the importance of using appropriate words for effective communication
keyInquiryQuestions: What strategies can you use to make effective oral presentations?
learningExperiences: Watch an audio visual clip on common places where they buy things and say them out loud (e.g. 书店、衣服店、食品店、药店、鞋店、市场)
Categorise items according to the places they can be bought with peers
Listen to a recording and make simple sentences using key expressions and vocabulary on the market place (老板、要多少?、多少钱?、零、买、卖)
Role-play asking the prices of items in the marketplace collaboratively
Use picture or words prompts related to the marketplace (e.g. 水果、蔬菜、钱、药) to make short oral presentations in turns
Work jointly with peers to research and talk about common places where they buy things in their neighbourhood
Discuss the importance of budgeting while buying items from the marketplace
coreCompetencies: Critical thinking and Problem solving: The learner carries out a research on the common market places found in their neighbourhood and talks about them.
Communication and Collaboration: Teamwork skills are displayed as the learner participates actively on the role play related to prices of items with peers.
linkedLearningAreas: Pre-technical Studies — prudent management of financial resources
subStrands.notes: 6 shop types (书店/衣服店/食品店/药店/鞋店/市场), marketplace transaction vocabulary (老板/要多少/多少钱/零/买/卖), 4 item categories (水果/蔬菜/钱/药).

subStrands.name: Phonological Awareness — Articulation
specificLearningOutcomes: Articulate words accurately in texts
Express their ideas clearly in spoken language
Appreciate the role of speaking clearly in enhancing communication
keyInquiryQuestions: How do you enhance clarity when responding to questions?
learningExperiences: Work jointly to pick random dates on a calendar and say them using the right sequence (年、月、日)
Listen to an audio clip and repeat the names of the holidays and festivities (圣诞节、情人节、新年、劳动节、独立日、自治日 (zìzhìrì))
Work with peers to discuss why the given dates are celebrated
Take turns to practise counting numbers with peers
Take turns asking each other their dates of birth (e.g. 你的生日是几月几号?)
Play spin a wheel game and answer the questions with peers
Work collaboratively to research online or offline on customs observed during the highlighted dates and share their findings
Reflect on their oral communication skills and identify strengths, weaknesses and areas of improvement
coreCompetencies: Learning to Learn: The learner reflects on their oral communication skills and highlights areas to make adjustments.
Digital Literacy: The competency is promoted as the learner connects and uses the internet to get information on customs observed in various holidays and festivities.
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — celebrating national holidays to express patriotism
subStrands.notes: Date sequence order 年/月/日 (year-month-day), 6 named holidays/festivities (圣诞节 Christmas/情人节 Valentine's/新年 New Year/劳动节 Labour Day/独立日 Independence Day/自治日 Madaraka-equivalent self-rule day), birthday question pattern 你的生日是几月几号?

subStrands.name: Phonological Awareness — Vocabulary Development, Articulation and Intonation
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify key words and phrases in varied listening texts
Discuss various topics using appropriate phrases and expressions
Display enthusiasm in using appropriate language for effective communication
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you speak clearly and effectively on various topics?
learningExperiences: Listen and repeat saying words and phrases related to when they undertake leisure activities (周末、每天、每个星期、每个月、放假的时候)
Team up with peers to recall vocabulary related to leisure time activities and draw a mind map
Use pictures/drawings to make oral presentations on activities they undertake during their leisure time
Take turns responding to questions on when they undertake their leisure activities (e.g. 你什么时候听音乐? 我周末听音乐 etc.)
Brainstorm and list positive and negative leisure time activities with peers
Collaborate with peers to present a skit on the importance of engaging in positive leisure activities for recreation
coreCompetencies: Critical Thinking and Problem solving: The learner applies evaluation and decision making skills as they highlight positive and negative leisure time activities.
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts and Sports — the concept of different leisure time activities
subStrands.notes: 5 time/frequency expressions (周末/每天/每个星期/每个月/放假的时候), question-answer pattern 你什么时候听音乐? 我周末听音乐.

subStrands.name: Listening for Information — Active Listening, Comprehension
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline vocabulary related to the theme from a text
Extract key information from a text
Acknowledge the role of grasping key information in communication
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you obtain the key points in oral communication?
learningExperiences: Listen to a recording and match pictures of food shopping places to their appropriate names (肉店、面包店、蔬菜店、超市、饭店)
Take turns saying the items listed in a shopping list (鸡肉、牛肉、羊肉、猪肉、面包、蛋糕、饼干、米饭、面条、大饼)
Watch a video clip on shopping for food and answer corresponding questions
Simulate different shopping situations incorporating acquired vocabulary and quantities (斤、公斤) with peers
Arrange the words given in the right sequence after listening to a recording on shopping experiences
Collaborate with peers to research and make presentations on the importance of using a shopping list in the marketplace
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: Team work skills are developed as the learner makes presentations of their research findings on the importance of shopping lists.
Learning to Learn: The learner works collaboratively with peers to simulate different shopping situations.
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — measurements and counting
Pre-technical Studies — budgeting through use of shopping lists
subStrands.notes: 5 food shopping places (肉店/面包店/蔬菜店/超市/饭店), 10 food items (鸡肉/牛肉/羊肉/猪肉/面包/蛋糕/饼干/米饭/面条/大饼), 2 quantity units (斤/公斤).

subStrands.name: Oral Expression — Vocabulary and Language Use, Articulation (Clarity)
specificLearningOutcomes: Choose suitable vocabulary for different speaking situations
Make accurate descriptions in interactions
Enhance self-esteem through communication
keyInquiryQuestions: How can fluency be enhanced in communication?
learningExperiences: Sing 'the body parts song' while simultaneously pointing to the corresponding part of the body with peers
Repeat saying descriptive words and phrases related to physical attributes after a listening prompt (e.g. 高、矮、黑、胖、瘦、长、短、大、小、帅、好看 etc.)
Take turns to describe their peers according to their physical attributes using "很" (e.g. 这是大卫。大卫很好看。他不矮，眼镜很大，头发很黑。)
Describe their friend's physical attributes using the negating verb "不" (e.g. 他不高 etc.)
Discuss how the choice of words when making descriptions can be used to foster positive self-image
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner describes their peers and friend's physical attributes using appropriate language, expression and gestures.
linkedLearningAreas: English and Kiswahili — use of appropriate words, phrases and expressions for effective oral communication
subStrands.notes: 10 physical-attribute descriptive adjectives (高/矮/黑/胖/瘦/长/短/大/小/帅/好看). Grammar pattern: 很 (very, for positive statement) vs 不 (not, for negation) with adjectives — e.g. 他很高 vs 他不高.

subStrands.name: Interactive Speaking — Intonation, Vocabulary and Language Use
specificLearningOutcomes: Use appropriate intonation and pace in oral communication
Apply appropriate vocabulary for specific communicative functions
Appreciate the role of interactive speaking for effective communication
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is vocabulary important?
How do you articulate your thoughts clearly when communicating?
learningExperiences: Listen to a poem on weather patterns and express the words and phrases with the correct intonation and pace (晴天、雨天、风天、阴天)
Present pictures of the different seasons and name them orally in turns (秋天、冬天、夏天、春天、旱季、雨季)
Collaborate with peers to sing a song on the various seasons
Watch a video clip of the clothes worn in various seasons and answer the related questions (T恤、短裤、毛衣、外套、大衣、雨衣、帽子、手套、围巾、靴子、凉鞋、太阳镜、游泳衣)
Research on seasons and weather patterns in Kenya and China and share the findings
Take turns to play seasons vocabulary charades for their peers to guess the correct season based on the actions
coreCompetencies: Critical thinking and Problem solving: The learner enhances their researching skills as they look for information on seasons and weather patterns in Kenya and China.
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — weather patterns and seasons
subStrands.notes: 4 weather-pattern words (晴天/雨天/风天/阴天), 6 season/climate-period words (秋天/冬天/夏天/春天/旱季/雨季), 13 clothing items (T恤/短裤/毛衣/外套/大衣/雨衣/帽子/手套/围巾/靴子/凉鞋/太阳镜/游泳衣). Kenya-vs-China weather comparison is an explicit sanctioned cross-cultural research prompt.

subStrands.name: Listening for Information — Active Listening and Participation
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify key vocabulary from a listening context
Organize their ideas logically and coherently in conversations
Acknowledge the significance of effective listening in communication
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we avoid distractions in a listening context?
learningExperiences: List the names of common areas or facilities in their locality after the recording (e.g. 医院、教堂、清真寺、面包店、超市、邮局、饭店、肉店)
Listen to descriptions and give the correct name of area/facility (e.g. 买饭的地方叫......，看病的地方叫.....)
Listen to a recording and fill in the gaps with the correct location words (对面、后面、附近、前面、旁边)
Listen to the given short text and answer the subsequent questions
Take turns to use the given map to describe the locations of different areas and facilities in the neighbourhood
Work jointly to give the locations of hidden treasures in their classroom
coreCompetencies: Citizenship: The learner communicates and collaborates within diverse teams when they take turns to describe locations in their neighbourhood using maps.
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — map reading to give directions
subStrands.notes: 8 neighbourhood facilities (医院/教堂/清真寺/面包店/超市/邮局/饭店/肉店), 5 location/relative-position words (对面/后面/附近/前面/旁边).

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud — Pronunciation (Tones)
specificLearningOutcomes: Pronounce words, phrases and sentences with correct tones
Read varied texts with accurate pronunciation
Show interest in reading a variety of texts for proficiency
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is mastery of pronunciation key in effective communication?
learningExperiences: Read vocabulary on informal greetings correctly and proficiently (吃了吗? 你今天怎么样? 你最近怎么样? 最近好吗? 大家好)
Chant a poem on numbers 1-100 with an appropriate tune collaboratively
Organise a scavenger hunt on vocabulary related to greetings and introductions and read them out
Take turns picking a card with clues about their peers and read them out as others guess who it describes (i.e. 叫什么名字?，多大了?，家人?，住在哪儿?)
Read aloud short texts on introduction of self and friend's (name, age and place of residence) for peer feedback
Work together to propose solutions to the reading challenges identified
coreCompetencies: Critical thinking and Problem solving: Interpretation and inferencing skills are exhibited as the learner explores possible solutions to the identified reading problems with peers.
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — counting and numbers
subStrands.notes: Same informal greeting register as 1.1 plus clue-card question forms (叫什么名字?/多大了?/家人?/住在哪儿?) — reading modality of the same theme content.

subStrands.name: Reading for Understanding — Inferencing, Comprehension
specificLearningOutcomes: Infer the meaning of key words and phrases from text
Express the main idea from texts
Exhibit a positive attitude towards reading
keyInquiryQuestions: How does expressing main ideas in a text enhance communication?
learningExperiences: Complete the blanks with the appropriate words/phrases related to titles of nuclear family members and professions
Read a text on introductions of nuclear family members and their professions and find unfamiliar words
Use a dictionary/other resources to find the meaning of the unfamiliar words and create a word wall collaboratively
Read a dialogue and answer the corresponding questions
Take turns to read short texts related to nuclear family members and assign an appropriate title for each of them
Establish a reading corner to foster a reading culture in the classroom with peers
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn: The learner is motivated to learn continuously when they establish a reading corner to promote a positive reading culture.
Creativity and Imagination: The learner undertakes group activities that inspire creative thinking as they create a word wall from the unfamiliar words identified.
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts and Sports — creatively expressing one's ideas
subStrands.notes: Reuses the nuclear family (10 titles) + 6 professions vocabulary from 1.2 in a reading-comprehension/dialogue format.

subStrands.name: Reading for Understanding — Active Listening, Comprehension
specificLearningOutcomes: Point out main information from texts
Respond accurately to questions in different contexts
Acknowledge the importance of price comparison before buying goods
keyInquiryQuestions: What does reading for understanding entail?
learningExperiences: Highlight vocabulary related to common places where they buy things from reading texts
Team up with peers to read the prices of items (元/块、先令) as labelled in the pictures/drawings/paintings
Read a role-play on asking for the prices of different items and fill the blanks using the appropriate key expressions and vocabulary (e.g. 老板、多少钱、买、卖)
Read a short passage and answer questions related to the context
Sequence words and phrases to form correct sentences
Discuss with peers why it is important to compare prices before purchasing items at the market
coreCompetencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The learner demonstrates that they can follow simple instructions to complete tasks by sequencing words and phrases to form correct sentences.
Communication and Collaboration: The learner exhibits teamwork skills as they participate actively in the discussion on why price comparison is essential when buying items at the market.
linkedLearningAreas: Pre-technical Studies — comparing prices to prudently utilise one's financial resources
subStrands.notes: Adds two currency terms (元/块 yuan, 先令 shilling) to the marketplace vocabulary from 1.3, plus a price-comparison financial-literacy application angle.

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud — Vocabulary Development, Fluency and Pace
specificLearningOutcomes: Derive the meaning of words when reading aloud
Apply appropriate fluency and pace in reading tasks
Appreciate the importance of pronouncing words clearly when reading aloud
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is correct pronunciation important in effective communication?
learningExperiences: Read aloud a short text highlighting holidays and festivities (圣诞节、情人节、新年、劳动节、独立日、自治日 (zìzhì rì)) as their peers mark any unfamiliar words
Work jointly to research the meanings of the words and share their findings
Read short poems related to important dates with the appropriate pace
Work with peers to read and count numbers aloud
Rearrange sentences related to birth dates and take turns reading them aloud in the correct sequence
Use flashcards to respond to the prompts on their dates of birth for critique by peers
Record themselves reading texts related to important dates and identify where they need help
Discuss how to safely use dictionaries or online resources to look up unfamiliar words or undertake tasks
coreCompetencies: Digital Literacy: Digital citizenship is promoted when the learner discusses how to be safe and responsible users of technology when undertaking various reading tasks.
Learning to Learn: The learner reflects on their own work as they record their reading to identify where they need help.
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — important national days
subStrands.notes: Same 6 holidays/festivities as 1.4, reading-fluency modality.

subStrands.name: Guided Reading — Comprehension, Word Recognition
specificLearningOutcomes: Recall factual information related to the text
Respond to questions from a text for comprehension
Appreciate the value of reading for lifelong learning
keyInquiryQuestions: How does reading foster a positive attitude toward language learning?
learningExperiences: Identify activities undertaken during leisure time from reading texts (唱歌、听音乐、看电影、看电视、看书、画画、旅游、打球、玩电脑游戏)
Fill the missing gaps with the appropriate words and phrases depicting time and frequency (周末、每天、每周、每个星期、每个月、放假的时候)
Read the passage related to when leisure time activities are undertaken and answer the questions
Organize a reader's theatre to read texts based on leisure time activities
Team up with peers to discuss the importance of undertaking positive fun and enjoyment activities
coreCompetencies: Citizenship: The learner engages in critical and constructive dialogue with peers to explore the value of engaging in positive leisure time activities.
Learning to Learn: The learner is motivated to learn continuously when they organise a reader's theatre to improve their reading proficiency.
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — management of one's leisure time
subStrands.notes: 9 leisure activities (唱歌/听音乐/看电影/看电视/看书/画画/旅游/打球/玩电脑游戏) — a larger, reading-specific pool than 1.5's oral set (休息/运动/逛街/和朋友聊天), plus the same 6 time/frequency expressions (note: 每周 and 每个星期 both appear as near-synonyms 'every week').

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud — Word Recognition, Intonation and Tone
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify key words related to the theme from texts
Read simple texts with proper intonation and tone
Appreciate reading texts for vocabulary enrichment
keyInquiryQuestions: How do presentations help in improving communication skills?
learningExperiences: Read short texts and match pictures of food items to their names (鸡肉、牛肉、羊肉、猪肉、面包、蛋糕、饼干、米饭、面条、大饼)
Read sentences and fill the blanks with the appropriate shopping places for different items (肉店、面包店、蔬菜店、超市、饭店)
Read short descriptions and categorise the food items with the corresponding places they can be bought with peers
Take turns reading simple dialogues on quantities of items (斤、公斤) for critique on intonation and tone by peers
Pick a card and read the text related to it with the appropriate tone and intonation
Work jointly to explore and discuss the different career prospects in the food and drinks industry
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: The learner exhibits team work skills as they categorise the food items correctly with their peers.
linkedLearningAreas: Pre-technical Studies — shopping for different items
subStrands.notes: Same 10 food items + 5 shops + 2 quantity units as 1.6, reading modality; adds an explicit categorise-by-place activity (item -> which of the 5 shops sells it) and a career-prospects discussion prompt.

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud — Articulation and Expression
specificLearningOutcomes: Express words with accurate pronunciation while reading aloud
Read simple texts with the appropriate articulation and expression
Display an interest in reading aloud effectively for communication
keyInquiryQuestions: How do you effectively convey expression when reading aloud?
learningExperiences: Identify and say aloud words and phrases depicting physical attributes from sentences (e.g. 高、矮、黑、胖、瘦、长、短、大、小) while paying attention to the tones
Read a passage on descriptions of physical attributes and answer the questions (e.g. 男生长得怎么样？男生很/不高，老师矮不矮？老师很矮)
Read simple sentences describing one's physical attributes using 很 and 不 (e.g. Nuru 很高，Nuru 的头发很长，Nuru 不高，Nuru 的头发不长)
Take turns reading aloud interrogative sentences on physical attributes
Read aloud the physical attributes of one of their peers as others make a drawing based on the description collaboratively
Reflect on personal reading aloud skills and identifying areas for improvement
coreCompetencies: Self-efficacy: The learner defines their personal skills as they reflect and identify areas of improvement in their reading skills.
linkedLearningAreas: English and Kiswahili — proper articulation and expression in enhancing reading proficiency
subStrands.notes: Same 9-10 physical descriptor adjectives and 很/不 grammar pattern as 1.7; adds possessive-attribute sentences (的头发 'X's hair') and interrogative forms (矮不矮? A-not-A question pattern).

subStrands.name: Reading for Fluency — Reading Strategies, Fluency
specificLearningOutcomes: Cite key words and phrases using appropriate reading strategies
Read simple texts on given topics fluently
Appreciate reading silently to enhance fluency
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you enhance understanding of texts when reading?
learningExperiences: Describe seasons and weather patterns depicted in the pictures using key words and phrases (e.g. 冷 lěng、凉 liáng、暖 nuǎn、热 rè、炎热 yánrè、雨季 yǔjì、旱季 hànjì、冬天 dōngtiān、春天 chūntiān、秋天 qiūtiān、夏天 xiàtiān)
Work with peers to circle words and phrases related to different types of clothing items used in various seasons from a word search
Scan through a weather report on a newspaper or digital device and highlight words and phrases related to weather and season
Take turns reading simple texts on weather and seasons for fluency
Describe the scenes depicted in the pictures given for review by peers on their fluency
Create reading groups in class and read texts on various themes of interest to develop their reading fluency
coreCompetencies: Creativity and Imagination: The learner establishes strong networking skills as they undertake group activities and exchange ideas on how to identify words from a word search.
Learning to Learn: This is promoted as the learner builds on their own learning experiences through the peer review on fluency.
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — varied weather patterns and seasons in the environment
subStrands.notes: Adds 5 weather-intensity adjectives with pinyin supplied by the curriculum itself (冷/凉/暖/热/炎热 = cold/cool/warm/hot/scorching-hot) to the 4 weather-pattern + 6 season words from 1.8, plus the 13-item clothing list reused via word-search.

subStrands.name: Reading for Understanding — Vocabulary Development, Reading Comprehension
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify key words and phrases from reading texts
Read simple texts on given topics for comprehension
Acknowledge the role of reading in building vocabulary
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is reading important?
learningExperiences: Highlight words on common areas or facilities found in their locality from a crossword puzzle (医院、教堂、清真寺、面包店、超市、邮局、饭店、肉店)
Use pictures or drawings to read the location of different areas and facilities in their neighbourhood
Take turns reading the location of different areas and facilities in their locality using the location words 对面、后面、附近、前面 and 旁边
Reading aloud a simple text and respond to related questions
Read short texts on areas or facilities in their neighbourhood and assign the correct picture to the appropriate text
Read the location of various areas and facilities while their peers draw what they hear
Form a reading buddy club to mentor and model reading among peers
coreCompetencies: Critical Thinking and Problem solving: The learner develops active listening and communication skills when they listen to the instructions given by their peers and draw maps to various areas and facilities in their neighbourhood.
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — map reading in giving directions
subStrands.notes: Same 8 facilities + 5 location words as 1.9, reading modality with a picture-to-text matching and dictation-drawing activity.

subStrands.name: Guided Writing — Handwriting (Legibility and Neatness), Grammar
specificLearningOutcomes: Compose grammatically correct sentences in writing tasks
Write legibly and neatly in Chinese
Show enthusiasm in writing clearly for effective communication
keyInquiryQuestions: What role does handwriting play in communication?
learningExperiences: Listen to an audio recording and list words and phrases related to informal greetings
Fill in the blanks with the appropriate words from a given text
Work with peers to decide whether the sentences given in a text are true or false
Compose simple texts on introduction of oneself and friends (name, age, place of residence)
Collect printed words and phrases from various sources and arrange the letters/words to make unique pieces of art/poetry on introduction of self and others
Share the creations with others for peer role modelling
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: The learner writes clearly and correctly simple texts on introduction of oneself and their friends.
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts and Sports — expressing oneself through various artistic forms

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING (confirmed against the PDF's own SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUB STRANDS table on page x and all 27 per-theme strand tables on pages 1-58, per CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md step 3 verification): Grade 7 Mandarin DOES follow the same 9-theme x 3-strand = 27-sub-strand count as Grade 8/Grade 9 Mandarin and French/German Grade 8 (9 themes: Greetings and Introduction, Family, My Surroundings, Time, Fun and Enjoyment, Foods and Drinks, My Body, Weather and Environment, Getting Around; repeated identically across Listening & Speaking (1.1-1.9), Reading (2.1-2.9), and Writing (3.1-3.9)). HOWEVER it DIVERGES from Grade 8/9's pattern in one respect worth flagging: Grade 8/9 use a UNIFORM sub-strand-type label per strand (e.g. every Grade 8 Listening & Speaking sub-strand happened to vary in specific title, but Reading sub-strands were consistently framed as fluency/understanding pairs). Grade 7 explicitly names FOUR DIFFERENT sub-strand types within Strand 1.0 alone per its own front-matter summary table (Oral expression / Phonological awareness / Listening for information / Interactive speaking) and rotates through them non-uniformly across the 9 themes (Oral Expression: themes 1,2,3,7; Phonological Awareness: themes 4,5; Listening for Information: themes 6,9; Interactive Speaking: theme 8) rather than one label per strand — confirmed by reading each of the 9 per-theme tables individually rather than assuming uniformity from the front-matter summary table alone (the summary table itself only gives aggregate lesson counts per sub-strand type: Oral expression 12, Phonological awareness 6, Listening for information 6, Interactive speaking 2 for Strand 1; Reading aloud 6, Reading for understanding 4, Guided reading 4, Reading for fluency 2 for Strand 2; Guided writing 9, Exhibitions and Showcase 6 for Strand 3 — the per-theme numeric codes 1.1-1.9/2.1-2.9/3.1-3.9 and their individual type labels are read from the 27 per-theme tables, the more specific and authoritative source, exactly as was done for Grade 8/9 Mandarin and French/German). This does not change the skill count (still 27, one per theme x strand) but does mean each skill's title/description should reflect its own theme-specific sub-strand type label rather than a strand-uniform one. No explicit 'Note: avoid...' exclusions were found anywhere in the design; no scopeNotes entries were populated for that reason. Register note: Grade 7's Greetings theme uses INFORMAL greetings (吃了吗/你今天怎么样/大家好) throughout, distinct from Grade 8's formal register (您好/您贵姓) — content is freshly mined from this PDF's own suggested-learning-experience examples, never copied from Grade 8.
